protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: In affected releases, authenticated admin CMS create/update accepts raw html_content, PageRepository only rewrites '=>' to '=>', and the storefront emits the stored value with Blade raw output {!! $page->html_content !!}. An intercepted request therefore bypasses TinyMCE and persists script-capable HTML that executes when rendered. GitHub's reviewed advisory and the PUBLISHED CVE record identify this stored-XSS mechanism and versions < 2.3.10.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CORRECTION_REQUIRED: b1285fa2433f58f7ea6d3eeee363876b8d471fe2 introduced unsanitized CMS persistence, but its storefront one-column template used escaped Blade output {{ $data['content'] }} and did not yet contain the vulnerable raw-output sink. Its direct child 9ca97aa594f44b0ee1e39fd2ed78c804d78013fd retained the unsanitized persistence and first added packages/Webkul/Shop/src/Resources/views/cms/page.blade.php with {!! DbView::make($page)->field('html_content')->render() !!}; this is the smallest public commit that first completes the exploitable source-to-store-to-sink lifecycle.

That parent lacks packages/Webkul/Shop/src/Resources/views/cms/page.blade.php, and its existing CMS storefront output is Blade-escaped, so the raw rendering sink and complete stored-XSS lifecycle are absent immediately before the corrected BIC.

corrected_fields.flaw_origin: Unsanitized CMS persistence first appeared in b1285fa2433f58f7ea6d3eeee363876b8d471fe2, but that parent's storefront template escaped the content. Commit 9ca97aa594f44b0ee1e39fd2ed78c804d78013fd immediately followed it, retained raw request persistence, renamed the field to html_content, and first added a Blade raw-output storefront sink.
